newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania national railway company plans concessions.
newsitem.headline: Romania national railway company plans concessions.

text.p: Romania's railway authority SNCFR said on Tuesday it was planning concessions of railway sectors in a bid to pull in domestic and foreign capital to upgrade the country's infrastructure.

"As the state's low budget resources cannot provide for the development of modern railway infrastructures at present and in the next few years...it is necessary to attract foreign and domestic capital to this sector," a SNCFR statement said.
It said SNCFR had worked out plans for concessions of three railway sectors, including electrification, upgrading and double-tracking.
The plans are yet to be sent to government for approval.
SNCFR said it intended to offer concessions for another 14 railway sectors in the future.
"By granting concessions SNCFR seeks to upgrade railway passenger and freight transport, as well as links with other European railway networks," the statement said.
Romania's railway infrastructure was badly neglected under the communists, who were ousted in 1989, and little has been done to improve its condition over the past six years.

According to SNCFR sources some 900 km (560 miles) of the railway network, which extends on over 11,000 km (7,000 miles), are in need of immediate repairs, along with at least half the country's 6,000 railway cars.
In July, Romania got a European Bank for Reconstruction and Development $72.6 million loan to upgrade its railway network.

The EBRD money, to be spent on upgrading rolling stock, will complement a $120 million credit pledged by the World Bank to improve dilapidated tracks and some $20 million from the European Union to renovate signalling systems.
The broader project was estimated at up to $410 million, including SNCFR's own funding.
According to official estimates, Romania needs around $30 billion to upgrade and develop its road, rail, air and sea transport by the year 2005. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
